title: Indian Army TES 57 2026: 90 Posts, Eligibility & Dates
metaDescription: Indian Army TES 57 2026: 90 posts, 10+2 PCM 60%, JEE Main 2026 mandatory, age 16.5-19.5. Apply by 12 November 2026 on joinindianarmy. Check now.
headline: Join the Indian Army Through TES 57

sections.title: What is the Technical Entry Scheme?
sections.content:
The 10+2 Technical Entry Scheme (TES) is a direct officer-entry route for young men who have completed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. Unlike the NDA, there is no written examination by UPSC. Shortlisting is based on Class 12 PCM marks and JEE Main participation, followed by the Services Selection Board interview.

TES-57 offers 90 provisional vacancies for the course commencing in July 2027. Selected candidates earn an engineering degree while training as Army officers and receive a permanent commission on completion. The vacancies are provisional and may increase or decrease according to organisational requirements.

sections.title: Eligibility: age and education
sections.content:
Candidates must be unmarried males aged between 16.5 and 19.5 years on 1 July 2027, which means a date of birth between 1 January 2008 and 1 January 2011, both dates inclusive. There is no age relaxation for any category, and only the date of birth on the Class 10 certificate is accepted.

Educationally, candidates must have passed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics and secured at least 60% aggregate marks in PCM, entered up to two decimal places without rounding. Appearing in JEE Main 2026 is mandatory. Candidates who meet the marks requirement but did not appear in JEE Main 2026 are not eligible.

sections.title: How to apply for TES-57
sections.content:
Online applications are accepted through the official website joinindianarmy.nic.in from 14 October 2026 to 12 November 2026, closing at 12:00 noon. Candidates must enter their exact PCM percentage and JEE Main 2026 details. Any false entry found at any stage leads to rejection and cancellation of candidature.

After applications close, the Army publishes a cut-off based on PCM marks and JEE Main performance. Shortlisted candidates are called for the five-day SSB interview, which includes psychological tests, group tasks and a personal interview, followed by a medical examination. The final merit list decides selection.

sections.title: Training, pay and career
sections.content:
Selected cadets train at the Indian Military Academy and affiliated technical institutions, completing an engineering degree alongside military training. On commissioning as Lieutenants, they serve in technical arms such as the Corps of Engineers, Corps of Signals and Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers.

Officers receive the standard Army pay scale with military service pay and allowances, plus accommodation, medical facilities and pension benefits. The technical entry offers a clear path to senior ranks, with further courses and specialisation available throughout a career that can span decades.
